intro: Sixteen questions, about ten minutes. It recommends where to start; it locks nothing. Choose "Not sure" rather than guessing: a guess that happens to be right sends you past something you'd benefit from.

questions.q: A price column holds "$1,299.00", "N/A" and blanks. Which order of steps loads it as a number with no errors?
o: Change the type to Decimal first, then remove errors
Replace "$" and "," with nothing and "N/A" with null, then change the type
Split the column by "$", then change the type
Filter out the rows that contain "$"
questions.why: Clean the text first, then convert. Converting first creates errors, and removing errors deletes real rows.

questions.q: In a star schema, which statement is true?
o: Fact tables filter dimension tables
Every table should relate to every other table
Dimension tables filter the fact table through one-to-many relationships
Bi-directional filtering is the recommended default
questions.why: Filters flow from the one side (dimension) to the many side (fact). Bi-directional is the exception, not the default.

questions.q: Why is Total Sales usually a measure rather than a calculated column?
o: Calculated columns can't be formatted as currency
A measure is evaluated in the current filter context when the visual asks, and doesn't store a value on every row
Measures are computed at refresh, so they are faster
Only measures can be used in slicers
questions.why: Measures respond to filters at query time. Calculated columns are computed at refresh and stored per row, which costs memory and doesn't react to slicers.

questions.q: You fix a report and publish it to the workspace, but people using the app still see the old version. Why?
o: Their browser cache needs clearing
App users only see changes after someone selects Update app
They need a Pro licence to see changes
The scheduled refresh failed
questions.why: An app is a published snapshot of workspace content. Workspace changes reach app users when the app is updated.

questions.q: Against SQL Server, which step is most likely to stop query folding?
o: Filtering rows on a date column
Removing columns
Renaming a column
Adding a column that calls a custom M function on every row
questions.why: Most built-in steps translate to SQL. A custom function invoked per row usually can't, so everything after it runs in the mashup engine.

questions.q: Budget is stored per Month and Product Category. Actuals are per day and product. How should Budget relate to the model?
o: Relate Budget to DimProduct[ProductKey] directly
Relate it at its own grain: to a Category-level dimension (or with TREATAS) and to a month-level date attribute
Copy budget onto every sales row in Power Query
Use a many-to-many relationship on ProductName
questions.why: A fact must join at its grain. Budget has no product or day, so it relates to the attributes it does have.

questions.q: In a matrix row for Color = Blue, what does CALCULATE([Sales], Product[Color] = "Red") return?
o: Blank
Sales for Blue
Sales for Red, because the filter argument replaces the Color filter from the row
Sales for Red and Blue together
questions.why: A boolean filter argument overwrites the existing filter on that column. KEEPFILTERS would intersect it instead and give blank.

questions.q: When does a scheduled refresh need an on-premises data gateway?
o: Always
When the source is on-premises or in a private network the Power BI service can't reach
Only for Excel files
Never for SQL Server
questions.why: Cloud sources reachable from the internet don't need one. On-premises or private-network sources do.

questions.q: A report page filter hides other regions from regional managers. Is that security?
o: Yes, if the report is shared through an app
No. Filters can be changed or bypassed (Build permission, Analyze in Excel). Use RLS roles
Yes, if the filter pane is hidden
Only for users without a Pro licence
questions.why: A filter is a presentation choice. Row-level security is enforced by the engine for every query, whatever the tool.

questions.q: Server Timings show 90% of the time in the formula engine and thousands of tiny storage engine queries. Most likely cause?
o: Too many columns in the model
An iterator evaluating a measure row by row, causing many storage engine requests (or callbacks)
A slow network between the browser and the service
The gateway is overloaded
questions.why: Thousands of small SE queries plus FE-heavy time is the signature of row-by-row evaluation. Rewrite so the storage engine aggregates in a few big queries.

questions.q: Which column usually costs the most memory in an Import model?
o: A Yes/No flag
A low-cardinality text column such as Region
A high-cardinality column such as a transaction ID or a datetime to the second
An integer foreign key with 50 values
questions.why: VertiPaq compresses by dictionary. Millions of distinct values mean a huge dictionary and poor compression.

questions.q: Some users may see every row but must not see the Salary column at all. Use:
o: Row-level security
Object-level security on the Salary column
Hide the column in the model
A perspective without Salary
questions.why: Hidden columns and perspectives are conveniences, not security. OLS makes the column not exist for that role.

questions.q: Why save a team's model as PBIP rather than PBIX?
o: The file is smaller
The model and report are saved as text (TMDL and PBIR) that Git can diff, review and merge
Refresh is faster
Apps require PBIP
questions.why: PBIX is a binary package. PBIP is a folder of documented text files, so changes can be reviewed and merged.

questions.q: Test and Production must read different source servers without anyone editing the file. Use:
o: Two copies of the PBIX
A parameter for the server plus a deployment rule (or variable) per stage
Edit the connection in Production after each deployment
Row-level security
questions.why: Parameters plus per-stage rules keep one artefact and make the environment difference explicit and repeatable.

questions.q: Which Direct Lake option never falls back to DirectQuery?
o: Direct Lake on SQL analytics endpoint
Direct Lake on OneLake
Both, when fallback is disabled in the gateway
Neither: all Direct Lake models can fall back
questions.why: Direct Lake on OneLake runs only in Direct Lake mode; conditions that would cause fallback make the query fail instead. Direct Lake on SQL can fall back.

questions.q: What does framing (refreshing) a Direct Lake model do?
o: Copies all the data into the model again
Points the model at the latest version of each Delta table, without copying data
Converts the model to Import mode
Sends a query to the SQL endpoint for every visual
questions.why: Framing reads Delta metadata. Columns load into memory later, when queries need them.
